text: Gauntlet started. Bar = 12 unique Steam 1080p shots in docs/ImageRefs/InfestedPlanet. Phase 1: engine, sprite bake, alien art line, world-look specs. Pieces are built by Opus 5.5, judged blind by Fable 5.1 critics, looped until ours wins.
Studying the factory line registry; building js/bugs.js (5 species, tripod gait, Aliens palettes), then baking drone/brute and a 600-bug swarm mock
Studying factory export (app.js buildSheet, humans line) to write tools/bake.js and pick a 5-marine roster + frame mech
Building WebGL2 batcher, fixed-step sim, input/camera, scenario registry, headless capture tool and a 3000-alien stress scenario

Studying the 12 IP shots + STYLE.md; writing tools/worldmock.py (procedural 1080p mocks for Olive Bog, Violet Basalt, and an own-twist spec), docs/WORLD-LOOK.md with palettes/prompts, then self-A/B vs ip_01/ip_02

Grok Imagine (grok.com/imagine) needs a sign-in; I can't create or use an account for you. The tab is open in the browser pane: sign in there and I'll generate the world-look example images from the spec prompts. Until then the examples are procedural mocks painted by tools/worldmock.py.

Built tools/bake.js (headless factory bake: tight buildSheet crop re-packed into square cells with the feet anchor centred, dusk look injected, refuses to write clipped sheets, plus --explore candidate sheets and --mocks review captures) and a 6-unit roster: rifle_a, rifle_b, sniper, fusion, medic in a shared violet/bone team palette at pitch 1.15 and size 0.75, plus one military-frame commander mech. Checked: none clipped, rebakes are byte-identical, idle marines are 30-48 px, about the size of ip_01's. Still weak: walk cycles barely read top-down (pauldrons hide the legs), the medic and rifles share a body, the sniper and fusion attack frames carry long built-in muzzle beams and flames, and there is no death animation.
judging

PICK NEEDED: three world-look specs in docs/WORLD-LOOK.md. (1) Olive Bog = ip_01/05 khaki wash + olive hair banks; (2) Violet Basalt = ip_02/09 near-black + magenta-rim rock + pink creep; (3) Cinder Tundra = our ash/rust/grave-moss/oxblood twist for the Mecha Factory dusk palettes. Self A/B: ref won all 6 pairs; ranking basalt > bog > cinder. Default if no answer: Violet Basalt first, Olive Bog second biome.

Built tools/worldmock.py (numpy/PIL painter: warped fBm wash ground, metaball banks with distance-field rim + tendril fringe, creep haze, gore splats, bug stream + patch, marine rings) and docs/WORLD-LOOK.md (palette tables sampled from the shots, materials, contrast ratios, risks, 9 Grok prompts, A/B results, recommendation). Verified by viewing all three 1080p mocks and the six blind A/B pairs. Still weak: bank interiors are noise not paint (the bar's hair/plane texture is the biggest gap), basalt rim is a uniform neon glow, bog ground is muddier than the bar's amber wash; units are stand-ins, no HUD in the mocks.
judging

Built js/bugs.js: 'bug' line (Aliens group), 5 species (drone/runner/spitter/brute/tank) x carapace/head/abdomen/markings/legs slots, tripod walk, lunge-bite / spit attack, idle twitch, 3 palettes (Infested Teal + Blood Hive, Void Brood). Baked at pitch 1.2 (1.0 showed side faces, legs hanging below the body): drone 20x19 px in 32 cell, brute 38x45 in 64, tank 64x67 in 96, none clipped; 1600 option combos build with no errors. Weak: shell still a bit more saturated/brighter than the JPEG bar, the bar's bugs merge into a softer mass while ours are discrete outlined stickers, brutes don't stand out in the swarm, mock river is thinner and less clumpy than ip_01.
judging

Blind A/B (ip_01 crop 1000,420,640,360): I picked A = the bar, narrowly. Ours are more legible as 'a soldier' but read as 3/4 pixel-art figures pasted onto a top-down map: helmet-over-chest-over-legs stacking, S facing is 42 tall x 33 wide with the gun 14 px below the feet anchor, hard 1-px black outlines on a soft painterly ground; the bar's marines are flat, soft, truly top-down and belong to their world. Biggest gap: presentation (pitch + hard pixel outline) reads as isometric sprites, not top-down marines. Other gaps: (2) soldier and fusion S/N walk does not read as walking: 8 S frames differ by only 12-33% of opaque pixels and it is all gun bob, legs hidden by shoulders (medic and mech walk fine); (3) fusion with pauldrons is a 48 px wide box with three bumps from S/N, the exact problem the builder fixed on the soldiers; (4) violet armour on the dark teal disc is low contrast, opaque mean luminance 75 vs bar marines with bright yellow-green highlights; (5) sniper idle is 21x23 px at S, the rifle only reads from E/N; (6) the scale mock uses flat noise ground so the A/B leaks the scene; paste onto a real ip_01 ground patch instead. Mechanics PASS: bake runs clean in 2 s into a fresh dir, byte-identical to the repo sheets, all 6 JSON have cellWidth/cellHeight/rows/columns/animations/anchor, no frame touches a cell edge, --cell=64 on fusion exits 1 without writing, 8 directions have consistent feet.

Would rather play the bar in all six blind pairs (ref won 6/6, ours identified every time). Closest pair: Violet Basalt vs ip_02, about 65/35 for the bar, not a near-tie. Biggest gap: the mocks' detail is unstructured noise where the bar's is drawn structure. Measured: mock ground HF_std 8-15 vs bar 2-3, mock bank interior 13 vs bar 3.5-4.3, i.e. ours is NOISIER at pixel scale while the bar is smoother but has lobes, 20-60 px curled strands and painted rock facets. The builder's diagnosis 'texture density' points the wrong way; more texture makes it worse. Other gaps: basalt rim is a uniform 35-54 px glow (peak magenta 66-74) on every rock where the bar varies 12 px line to 44 px bloom per rock (spec's 0.6-1.0 noise modulation on exp(-d/26) is the cause, needs 0-1 and a crisp 2 px line); basalt ground too violet/saturated (mock #251822 sat 93 vs bar #17161b sat 46, neutral charcoal); bog banks are flat olive blobs with no lobe volume and scribble fringe; bog ground is cold and dark vs the bar's amber wash; cinder has no identity. Specs are concrete (hex tables, recipes, creep, contrast ratios) and worldmock.py regenerates byte-identical PNGs. Ranking: Violet Basalt > Olive Bog > Cinder Tundra; default Violet Basalt.

Built Game/js/engine.js (WebGL2 batcher: 7 layers ground..over+screen, one VBO upload per flush, up to 8 textures per draw call, premultiplied alpha, additive draws that still batch, SDF discs/rings, dashed lines, polys/hexes, render targets for persistent decals; fixed 60 Hz accumulator; mulberry32 per scenario with IP.fork streams; unified pointer/touch/keys with tap/longpress/drag and pinch/middle-drag/WASD/edge/wheel camera clamped to the map; scenario+system registry; IP.assets sheet loader for factory meta; IP.capture), index.html, game.css (letterbox, safe areas, portrait rotate hint), tools/capture.js (own server, Metal GPU headless, --actions, --page phone shots) and README-engine.md. Verified: stress at t=5 is byte-identical across runs (Metal and SwiftShader); real rAF holds 60 fps at 3k aliens with 6 draws and ~1 ms cpu, 60 fps at 30k, 18 fps at 60k; pinch, longpress, tap, drag and the cancel-on-second-finger path were tested with CDP touch; the real bug_drone/bug_brute sheets load and animate; fixed a render-target feedback-loop bug and a pinch bug found while testing. Still weak: the stress art is placeholder (procedural bugs, blobby ground); the y-sort in JS costs ~1.5 ms at 30k; no render interpolation (sim and camera move at 60 Hz, so 120 Hz screens repeat frames); portrait phones get a small frame; system scripts that don't exist yet log 404s in the console.
Round 2: soften/antialias sprites (2x render + downsample, outline blend), steeper pitch study, fusion silhouette, walk sway, brighter palette, in-situ scale mock on ip_01 ground
judging
Round 2: replace noise detail with drawn structure (lobes, strands, rock facets), retune basalt/bog palettes, per-spec compositions, re-run A/Bs

Would rather fight the bar (A=ref, called before key). Biggest gap: at 1:1 our bugs read as bright royal-blue rectangles with 1px mint stick legs and a heavy black outline (28% near-black pixels in the dense crop vs 2% in the ref), not the ref's dark navy blobs with yellow-green head/leg-tip highlights. Second: swarm density; bug pixels cover 42% of our dense crop vs 80% in the ref, mock is one thin gappy ribbon. Third: brute is a stacked barrel and tank a block pile, both read as mechs. Fourth: shell too light and saturated (mean bug pixel 56,125,145 vs ref 43,84,92). Mechanics pass: bug line registered, all 5 species deploy, no page errors, 8 rows x 13 cols no empty cells, deterministic (md5 match on rebake), walk frames change 70-125 px per step and alternate tripods, attack reads as a lunge with jaws opening. Caveat: factory's own MFApp.buildSheet at cell 32 clips the drone (anchor y=29); only MF.Bugs.bakeSheet is safe.
Round 2: darker teal ovoid drones, soft shadow-edge outline, thick yellow-tipped legs, beetle brute/tank, dense two-stream + hive mock

PASS (engine, no visual A/B). Verified myself: two seeded captures byte-identical (md5 bb40fc6f...), exactly 1920x1080; identical again with --actions, on SwiftShader, and from a 1280x720 live window (capture is window-size independent). Real rAF loop 60 fps at 3000/6000/12000 aliens (0.9/1.7/4.1 ms CPU, 6 draw calls). Full DESIGN.md API present and working; 30/30 real-browser checks passed: WASD, edge scroll, middle-drag (consumed for systems), wheel zoom anchored under cursor and clamped, click/right-click/drag with world coords and origin, touch tap/longpress, two-finger pinch (first finger gets cancel) and two-finger pan, F3 overlay (DOM, not in captures), error isolation, renderTo orientation, bug_drone sheet parsing, phone portrait letterbox 390x219 + rotate hint, coarse-pointer budget 1500. Biggest gap: no engine-side y-sort for the unit layer, so marines/aliens/structures from different systems cannot interleave and every system pays its own JS sort (1.5 ms of 8.6 at 30k). Other gaps: no render interpolation (120/144 Hz and ProMotion phones get uneven 60 Hz cadence); IP.queueActions 'key' unshifts its keyup ahead of same-time actions (a click at t=1 next to a key at t=1 lands at tick 61 not 60, verified); negative sprite frame index gives NaN UVs instead of wrapping; IP.errors/errSeen never reset across loadScenario; no font shipped (hud's job but engine should ship the loader test); fps=60 is rAF-capped so cpu_ms is the real headroom number.

Request to orchestrator: please open a factory piece for a bigger top-down stride in js/humans.js (scale P.swing / P.lift when camera pitch > 1, or expose a stride multiplier on the blueprint). At pitch 1.4 the human legs mostly hide under the shoulders from S/N; bake only fakes it with a baked sway and does not own humans.js.

Built: bake renders every unit at 2x size and box-downsamples 2:1 (premultiplied), softens the outline colour to 60% outline + 40% body (0 opaque black rim px; 32-36% of rifle_a S edge px at alpha 0.2-0.9), bakes a walk sway (3 deg + 1 px perpendicular; fusion 4 deg/1.5 px), pitch 1.4 (picked from 1.15/1.3/1.4 study; 1.5 hides the legs), new roster: light/spiked shoulders, legLen 1.25 bulk 1.0, fusion light shoulders (S idle 36 px wide, flamer visible S/N), primary #6a56c8, bone #e4dfcc, steel #868ca0, one teal accent family, sniper size 0.85 at 160 cell, medic inverted. Scale mock now on ip_01 ground with marines covered (+ -scale-flat). Verified: 6 lines clipped=false, two clean bakes byte-identical, --cell=64 fusion exits 1 unwritten, opaque luminance 101-141 (medic lightest), rifle_a S idle 31x31, walk S/N neighbour change >= 0.35 for all units (thresholded diff), weapons within 26 px of meta.center. Weak: our marines read ~15% smaller than the bar's and lack its bright pink/teal top plate; rifle_b S idle 27x34 (gun hangs below); legs barely visible at 1.4 so the walk leans on sway; no death animation.
judging

Blind A/B (ip_01 crop 1000,420,640,360, verdict written before the key): I picked B = the bar. Biggest gap: at game scale ours are five identical mid-violet beetles, 31 px S idle body vs the bar's ~40 px marines (22% smaller, not 15%) and no bright identity cap: the bar's marines carry a hot-pink/teal top plate (sat 0.53, 115 hot-pink px in a 40x40 core) that reads from across the screen; ours are uniform violet (sat 0.39) with a bone trim too thin to see at 1:1. Other gaps: (2) the S/N walk is a whole-sprite 3 deg wobble, not legs: the 0.35-0.69 neighbour diff is the rotation, the legs never show from S on rifle_a/rifle_b (needs the humans.js stride piece; do not raise sway further); (3) attack frames bake VFX into the sprite: sniper 141 px muzzle beam (hence the 160 cell), fusion cyan flame cone, rifle muzzle flash; the vfx piece owns tracers and the bar's fusion is orange, so strip them and shrink cells; (4) the mock handicaps us: covered patch lum 46 vs the bar's ground 63, and 52 px rings vs the bar's 84-98 px rings; (5) rifle_b S idle 27x34 with the gun hanging 18 px under the feet; (6) no death frames. Real progress: pitch 1.4 and the 2x soften fixed round 1's pixel-art read; edges are antialiased (0 opaque black px), 8 facings are consistent, feet centred within 1 px (x offsets are the gun). Mechanics PASS: clean bake in 4 s, byte-identical rebake, --cell=64 fusion exits 1 unwritten, all 6 JSON complete, no frame touches a cell edge.
Round 3: size up to ~40px bodies, identity caps, strip baked VFX, fair mock, square rifle_b, A/B

Rebuilt bugs.js: faceted-ovoid bodies (dark blue abdomen + mint thorax hub + mint legs with yellow-green emissive tips), low-key finish in MF.Bugs.bakeSheet (no top outline, 150/70-alpha shell-dark shadow edge, despeckle), Infested Teal darkened, brute = wide banded beetle with pincers, tank = spiked dome. Measured densest 160x120: bug px 92.8% (ref 88.9% same metric), near-black 5.4% (ref 2.4%), mean (52,93,98) vs ref (43,82,89). Still weak: mint leg strokes read as slashes vs the ref's compact stars; hangar view keeps the raw renderer outline.
judging

Pick one world look before terrain art starts (default if no answer: Violet Basalt). 1 Olive Bog (ip_01/05): amber-khaki wash, lobed olive banks with lit rims, hair strands and bulb-tipped tendrils. 2 Violet Basalt (ip_02/09): neutral charcoal ground, faceted rock plateaus with a thin purple line and an uneven cloudy magenta bloom, violet creep. 3 Cinder Tundra (ours): ash slate, grave-moss banks with a bone rim, oxblood creep; kept on file. Specs with hex tables and stroke recipes in docs/WORLD-LOOK.md.

Rewrote tools/worldmock.py around drawn structure: bog banks are lobe metaballs with per-lobe lit rims, 2.5 px merged bumps, inner darkening, 36 px halo, 220-400 tapered strand strokes + dark curls along a flow field and bulb-tipped hooking tendrils (dab-painted at 2x, downsampled); basalt rocks are irregular polygons with bites, anisotropic Voronoi facets (4 flat levels, soft edges), painted seams, a 1.4 px purple line that never vanishes, a 0-1 cloudy bloom 9-30 px wide (crater forced to a solid ring); grounds are smooth washes with 100-300 px pools and dust speckle, no grain. Each spec has its own layout. Added --check (HF/MF, palette, rim widths). Verified: basalt clean ground (22,21,27) sat 58 HF 0.85 (bar (23,22,27) 46 0.85); rock interior HF 0.55 p10/p90 25/37 (bar 0.72, 27/40); rim width along the plateau 2-37 px with ~38% of contour bloom-free; bog dark ground (43,42,22) lit (54,53,27) p10-p90 ~20; bank HF 3.4-3.7; md5 identical on re-run. Self A/B (not blind, builder knows the layouts): ref 6/6, basalt vs ip_02 about 60/40 for the bar with the ground a near-tie and the rocks the gap; bog vs ip_01 about 70/30. Still weak: bog hair density MF 2.5-2.7 vs target 4-6, tendrils too evenly spaced, basalt facets cleaner than brushwork, crater ring wider/fuzzier than the bar's, stand-in units, no HUD.
judging

Would rather fight the bar (called A before reading key; A=ref). Biggest gap: at 1:1 our mass is a flat mint-slash mat, not the ref's grid of dark navy blobs each with one compact bright star. Measured in the densest 160x120 crop: bright mint pixels (g>120) 30% vs 12.7% in ip_01, very bright (g>150) 20% vs 3.4%, mint-dominant 30% vs 16%; the thorax hub plus six mint legs cover about half of each 20 px drone and the accent is scattered 1 px tips instead of one 4-5 px head cluster. Second: value/hue, lum std 36 vs 28 and shells read grey-teal where the ref's read blue. Third: brutes vanish inside the mass (same tint, no accent). Fourth: attack is a 2-3 px nudge with no wind-up or leg tuck. Fifth: hangar/factory preview still shows the hard outline and facet stripes. Mechanics pass: bug line registered, all 5 species deploy with no page errors, wrapped MFApp.buildSheet returns centered sheet (bakedWith MF.Bugs.bakeSheet, anchor 16,17), 8x13 cells none empty none touching the edge, S frames 20x20, deterministic (md5 df30952c matches the shipped file), walk diffs 77-116 px per frame with alternating tripods, 8 direction silhouettes consistent ovoids. Real progress from r1: they now read as organisms.
Round 3: dark-navy blob bodies with one compact head star, shell-tone legs, real lunge, magenta brute band, per-bug shade variants, ship all 5 sheets

Rather play the bar in all six blind pairs (keys confirmed; ours identifiable every time). Specs are now concrete enough to build from (hex tables, lobe/stroke/facet/bloom recipes, contrast rules) and md5s reproduce, but no mock is within striking distance: basalt vs ip_02 is about 65/35 for the bar on the ground alone, not a near-tie. Biggest gap: banks and rocks read as vector/airbrush construction, not paint. Basalt: a 1 px crisp neon contour line, 30-60 px Voronoi camo facets with a ruled seam scratch, and a floorless double-ring crater (2 magenta peaks per side on rows 300/320 vs the bar's 1). Bog: smooth sphere-shaded lobes with LIGHT line-art scribbles on top (the bar's hair is dark and dense; bank MF 2.5-2.7 vs 4-6) and 3 px uniform pin tendrils with dots (bar: 5-8 px tapered, soft, hooked, 3x denser). Other gaps: basalt clean ground is flat (p10/p90 20/24 vs bar 16/37) and emptier/darker frame-wide (median L 27 vs 34-37, sat 85 vs 100-122: the bar carries violet haze and 2-6 px blotch mottle over most of the frame); bog ground is murkier and less amber than ip_01/05 (median L 46 vs 53-55, amber pixels 32% vs 37-55%, open ground away from pools (42,46,25)); contrast table is asserted from hex, not measured on the mocks. Ranking: 1 Violet Basalt (default), 2 Olive Bog, 3 Cinder (file). Builder report swapped the bog/basalt md5s.

Built: S idle bodies are now 38-40 px wide (were 31). Each marine has a vivid cap: tools/bake.js repaints the helmet and pauldron nodes with its own non-pastel ramp (rifles pink, sniper cyan, fusion orange, medic white with red trim). Baked VFX are stripped (muzzleFlash is a no-op): attack reach is 29-38 px, the sniper's 54 px is the rifle itself. rifle_b now has big pauldrons, S box 48x45. Fairer mocks: our squad stands on the bar's own spots in ip_01 and ip_05. The bar's marines and rings are hidden by patch-matched, gain-matched discs, and region luminance is 64.9 vs the bar's 63.3. Rings match the bar as measured (outer radius about 27 px, not the 42 asked for). Rebake is byte-identical; all six units clipped=false. My A/B is not truly blind (I made the image): narrowly prefer ours on ip_01, prefer the bar on ip_05. Still weak: legs never show in the S walk (that needs the humans.js stride); the ip_05 bar marines are bigger and more heroic than ours; rifle_b's cap is 5x5 and the medic's is white only; no death animation.
judging

Blind A/B: picked the bar on BOTH pairs (ip_01 crop: A=ref chosen; ip_05 crop: B=ref chosen). Sheets are mechanically sound (bake deterministic, 12 files byte-identical on rerun, JSON has cellWidth/Height/rows/columns/animations/anchor, no clipping, cell=64 refuses correctly, 8 rows rotate consistently). Biggest gap: VALUE. Candy identity caps (hot-pink helmet + both pauldrons, white/red medic, orange) on a mid-violet body give S-idle median V 0.71-0.81 with 35-51% of pixels above V 0.8; the bar's marines are deep violet at median V 0.37 with 0% above 0.8 and only thin cyan edges. Ours read as stickers pasted on the ground, the bar's as armoured soldiers in it. Second: silhouette/pose. At pitch 1.4 each human is three boxes in a row (pauldron-helmet-pauldron) with the gun hanging diagonally off the side; the bar's are an angular chevron body with a long rifle held forward along the facing, so facing reads from the barrel. Third: medic is a white/red striped bar (E/W idle 25x49, reads as an ambulance). Fourth: walk is whole-sprite sway only (S-row neighbour diffs 274-731 px, no stride); needs js/humans.js. STYLE.md says low-saturation, one accent, hidden faces: the caps break that.

Drones are now dark navy-blue blobs with one compact 5x5 mint star at the front. Legs are 1px teal-grey, the forelegs share the mint head, and there are no glowing tips. The bake finish quantises to low-key tones with a navy shadow edge. There are 3 seeded shade variants, and brutes are darker with a full rim and a magenta membrane. The wind-up/thrust lunge moves 7px on the E row. All 5 sheets ship. On the densest mock crop every target is in range: bright 11.1, vbright 2.9, mint 14.3, blue 73, lumstd 30.1, near-black 3.1, mean 37,78,90. Brutes are 19 luminance darker than the drones around them. Weak: the per-sprite bright share is 11.5%, over the asked 8%, because that is what the crop target needs. Stars are crisper and smaller than the ref's soft clusters, and the hangar still shows the raw model.
judging

Would rather fight the bar (called B before the key; B=ref). Real progress: body hue/sat/value now match ip_01 (body mean 32,75,94 vs 36,75,87), bright share 11.3 vs 11.5 pct, sheets mechanically clean (8x13, nothing clipped, buildSheet bake md5 matches shipped, lunge reads). Biggest gap: every bug is identical, so the mass reads as a tiled carpet of navy pebbles with one pinpoint star each, not an organic swarm. Measured: body saturation std 0.09 vs ref 0.15; bright-blob median 14 px vs ref 5 px (ref mixes many 1-3 px pale-cyan specks with fewer soft 10-20 px green clusters; ours is one fixed 5x5 star per bug); highlight colour too green (104,157,123 vs ref 98,142,132); ground visible 0.7 pct vs 6.2 pct in the densest crop. Second: the shell is a flat silhouette with no internal form, 1 px leg nubs vanish at 1:1, so no bug reads as a creature. Third: walk cycle is near-static (only 1 px leg nubs change, 1 px bob). Fourth: hangar still shows the raw lit model, not the shipped finish.

Specs delivered in docs/WORLD-LOOK.md with three mocks (world-bog-r2, world-basalt-r2, world-cinder-r2). Critic's ranking: 1 Violet Basalt, 2 Olive Bog, 3 Cinder Tundra; none beat the bar yet (banks read as vector/airbrush, not paint). Decision while you're away: the terrain piece builds BOTH Basalt and Bog as biomes in-engine (basalt default), carrying the critic's round-3 recipe; python mocks stop here. Override any time by naming a biome.
Round 4: darken team palette to bar register, shrink cap to head, aim-pose idle, medic fix, topdown stride, ip_01 five-ring mock

Phase 1 done (18 agents, 71 min): engine PASSED 8/10 (60 fps at 12k sprites, byte-identical captures). Bake 3/10, alien-art 6/10, world-look 5/10 all lost their blind A/Bs; their critic to-dos carry into phase 2. Phase 2 launched: terrain (both biomes in-engine), swarm, marines, structures, vfx, hud as new loops, bake and alien-art continuing from round 4. Up to 3 rounds each, 8 loops in parallel.

Built Game/js/marines.js: 5-marine squad (sniper,rifle_a,fusion,rifle_b,medic sheets; sprite centred on meta.center), click/shift-click/box/1-5/Space,F2/double-click selection, right-click+longpress move, KeyA arm/modifier or flags.attackMove attack-move (red dotted line + arrow), KeyH hold, flowTo-steering with separation slots, auto-target via IP.swarm.nearest, rifle/sniper(pierce 2)/fusion cone/medic pistol+heal/rocket, shared world.ammo, HP+death, IP.marines API; segmented salmon ring + teal disc when selected, red pulsing when hurt, cyan dotted order lines, hp pip, contact shadow, y-sort. Verified: harness test of every selection/order path, touch tap+longpress capture, swarm+vfx integration, swarm-demo adoption, byte-identical reruns, stress exit 0. Weak: KeyA also pans the engine camera on maps larger than the frame; terrain flowTo not exercised (terrain.js absent); demo ground is a placeholder; marines never get hurt in the demo trickle.
judging

Built Game/js/hud.js: top-left magenta slashed-zero BP + skewed 11-cell AMMO bar on a navy band; 5 interlocking hex-cut marine cards (class name, striped red HP with green missing part, pixel weapon silhouettes; selected card drops 8px with a 6px cyan frame + blue top band; dead = grey DEAD + circled X); right rail of navy flat-top hexes with cached vector biohazards (tap opens name/desc panel, new mutation pulses + alerts); bottom-left build/squad/research and bottom-right attack-move/regroup/rocket clusters (toggles set world.flags, all presses emit 'ui'); fading centred alerts (auto on marine death, hive-captured, new mutation); ip_02 dialogue box with typewriter text, placeholder hex portrait, tap/Enter to advance, HUD hidden while it shows. Input: init() puts a gate at the front of world.systems so HUD presses are consumed before marines see them (verified: clicking buttons/cards issues no orders, world right-click still orders; selection via IP.marines.select). Verified: hud-demo/dialogue/states exit 0 with --systems=hud,marines, byte-identical reruns, 60 fps, stress exits 0. Weak: name/label font is Chakra Petch not the bar's rounder face; portrait is a flat placeholder; weapon silhouettes and biohazard are close but simpler than the bar's art; demo ground is a stand-in, not terrain.
judging

Built Game/js/vfx.js: tracers per weapon (rifle red triangle line + white head, sniper streak, fusion orange blobs, medic crosses, turret dots, rocket smoke), additive muzzle flashes, hit sparks, persistent grainy blood splats (core/mid/spray + hot accents, bead trails, droplets) painted into 2048 px render-target chunks drawn as one decal quad each, fading #1a0a14 corpses, white shred bursts for brute/tank, explosions (orange body + additive glow, ring, embers, smoke, big splat, scorch, deterministic shake), marine death splat + grey X, magenta hive-capture burst; vfx-demo + vfx-bench scenarios.
